subject: Microlinq — retention alternatives & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <epark@microlinq.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Microlinq — retention alternatives & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed path so we have alignment: 

Call summary (minutes)
- Microlinq primary ask: minimize retention of end-user content (PII present in prompts). Ideal outcome: no raw-text retention ("0-retention") for production inference.
- Secondary asks: short-term logging for billing/diagnostics, exportable audit evidence for compliance, and ability to restrict model residency to us-east-1.
- Constraint: Microlinq cannot accept wholesale loss of billing/usage metrics — need per-team monthly invoiceable usage.

Proposed compromise from Redwood (initial):
1) Ephemeral input storage: redact or drop any field labeled PII at ingest (customer-side tagging + optional server-side PII redaction) and do not retain raw prompt text past 5 minutes by default.
2) Metadata billing logs: retain non-PII metadata (request_id, model, token_counts, timestamp, hashed_user_id) for 30 days for billing & quota reconciliation. Hashing will be one-way (salted) to prevent re-identification.
3) Audit bundle option: for customers that need evidence, generate a time-limited, access-controlled audit bundle that contains pseudonymized interaction records for a configurable window (30/90 days) and only accessible to Microlinq security via mutual TLS.
4) Residency: host in us-east-1 Dedicated pool or Private VPC — we can enforce region pinning for inference.

Open items we need to confirm from your side:
- Which fields you consider PII (examples: full names, SSNs, email addresses vs. product IDs) — if you share a sample JSON schema we can bake redaction rules.
- Acceptance of hashed_user_id in billing logs (we cannot keep raw user identifiers for 30 days under the proposed compromise).
- Whether an audit bundle with pseudonymized content satisfies your internal auditors.

Next steps (I suggest):
- Microlinq to send the sample payload schema and priority PII fields (Elena/Tom) — due Tue 4/27
- Redwood to produce a short proposal with the exact retention windows, redaction approach, and estimated cost delta for the dedicated privacy configuration — due Fri 4/23 (we can accelerate if needed)
- Security sync between Microlinq sec@microlinq.ai and our Security team (Karthik) to schedule an evidence call.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (high level SOC2 letter), dap_v1_redlines.docx (initial DPA draft with a couple of flag comments)

If that looks right, I’ll put together the formal proposal and loop in Engineering for the residency/capacity estimate.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Park <epark@microlinq.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Microlinq — retention alternatives & next steps

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. Quick notes: 
- We will extract a sample payload schema and call out fields we consider PII (names, user_email, phone_number, raw transcripts) by Monday 4/26.
- One concern from Security: if you hash user IDs in logs, will you be able to support de-duplication for per-customer monthly quotas? We need to ensure billing aligns with those hashes.
- Latency question: if we enable the "ephemeral redaction" path + audit bundle generation, will that add to tail latency or change SLA? Important for our real-time flows.

Tom Suarez (cc) will also want to review the DPA redlines. We can schedule a 30-min sec sync after you send the proposal.

Thanks — Elena
Principal Product Manager, Microlinq

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Microlinq retention alternatives — engineering notes

Vivek / Marissa — a couple of technical clarifications to include in the proposal (pulled from Infra/Runtime):
- Hashing & billing: we can emit a hashed_user_id using a per-customer HMAC key. That will allow Microlinq and Redwood to map and de-duplicate consistently for billing while keeping the underlying PII out of logs. We'll include an HMAC key rotation plan in the SRE playbook.
- Latency impact: in-path redaction adds ~2-4ms median per-request (negligible) and up to ~15-20ms tail for large multi-page transcript redactions. Audit bundle generation is an asynchronous job — it will not affect inference SLOs if we queue it to an off-path worker. We'll call that out explicitly.
- Residency: Dedicated us-east-1 pool with network egress rules and encrypted storage for the short-term metadata is straightforward. Private deployment adds more lead time and licensing considerations.

I'll draft a short technical appendix we can attach.

— Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <epark@microlinq.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Microlinq — retention alternatives & next steps (commercial)

Elena — quick commercial note so you have transparency: the privacy-focused configuration (ephemeral raw text, metadata billing logs, audit-bundle on request, region pinning) will carry a ~18% uplift on our base per-token rates compared to our standard hosted offering. If Microlinq commits to Dedicated capacity (12mo minimum), we can reduce that uplift to ~8% and include advanced audit tooling as part of the contract.

I'll include a short pricing table in the formal proposal and flag the uplift to procurement. Happy to run numbers on your forecast if you share expected monthly token volume.

— Marissa
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Microlinq — retention alternatives & next steps

Elena / Microlinq Security team — following up with the formal proposal attached (Microlinq_privacy_proposal_v1.pdf) and the technical appendix Karthik mentioned. Highlights: 
- Default behavior: redact PII fields (per your schema) and drop raw prompt text after 5 minutes.
- Billing & reconciliation: emit salted HMAC hashed_user_id into metadata logs retained for 30 days. We can provide a signed per-month usage export for reconciliation.
- Audit evidence: one-click audit bundle generation (pseudonymized) — retention windows configurable to 30/90 days.
- Commercial: pricing uplift options and Dedicated discounting captured.

Requested actions from Microlinq:
1) Confirm sample schema (Elena) by 4/27
2) Security sync: propose Tue 4/28 10:00 AM PT (Karthik to join) — please confirm
3) Procurement: indicate whether you prefer a 12mo Dedicated commitment or pay-as-you-go hosted so we can finalize pricing

Attachments in this email: Microlinq_privacy_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), Microlinq_Security_Requirements.xlsx (your sheet we discussed)

Thanks — Vivek
